summary: This paper audits and mathematically sharpens the analytic endgame and logarithmic scale calculus of the formalized Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (lsernau/grh-lean). It proves three main pillars: (1) Linear-window collapse of the quadratic second-scale window [t, t^2] into an explicit linear window [t, lambda t] with linear moment order k = ceil(kappa t); (2) Exact closed-form solution of the two-barrier variational problem and determination of the sharp phase transition lambda_crit = max(1, (alpha + gamma)/delta_0); and (3) Sharpening of star_inequality (recovering a full factor of log b), prime-error exponent bounds, and exact integer LP characterization of New.grh divisor 51. All results are fully formalized in Lean 4 (0 sorry) and verified via an AST-audited zero-float rational interval verifier (16 SHA-256 certificates, 59/59 pytest tests).
strengths: Complete, formally verified Lean 4 implementation with 0 sorry, 0 warnings, and 0 custom axioms across 13 core theorems.
Bridges qualitative bounds to sharp quantitative polynomial second scales x^{lambda * 10^6} via linear-window collapse.
Exact closed-form solutions for left-barrier (rho* = 3e) and right-barrier variational saddles.
